name: Naha International Airport
before:
Okinawa's main airport, 4 km west of Naha city hall, and Japan's sixth busiest. It carried 21.5 million passengers in 2018 and runs 24 hours a day.

It is the hub for two airlines that matter for island hopping. Japan Transocean Air connects Okinawa to the rest of Japan, and Ryukyu Air Commuter links the main island to the surrounding islands, so most onward travel in the prefecture starts here.

International flights reach Taiwan, Hong Kong, South Korea, Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and mainland China.

The terminals were built in stages and are worth identifying before travel. The domestic terminal dates from 1999, a low cost carrier terminal was added as a north annex in 2012 for Peach services, and a new international terminal opened in 2014. The old domestic terminal became the cargo terminal in 2009.

Skytrax ranked it 91st in the world in 2024, up from 199th the year before, making it the most improved airport in the world that year.

The airport is also home to a Japan Air Self-Defense Force base.
after:
Okinawa's main airport, about 4 km west of central Naha. It handled about 23.5 million passengers in the year to March 2026 and runs 24 hours a day.

Ryukyu Air Commuter is based here and links the main island to the surrounding islands, so most onward travel in the prefecture starts here.

The terminal operator lists international flights to Taiwan, Hong Kong, South Korea, Thailand, Singapore and mainland China.

Its terminals were built in stages: the domestic terminal opened in 1999 and a new international terminal in 2014, and since 2019 a connecting building has joined the two.

Skytrax ranked it 61st in the world for 2026 (78th in 2025).

claims.claim: Japan's sixth busiest
claims.why: A 2018 ranking. MLIT's national ranking tables are Excel files the sweep's tools cannot save, and its readable sheets leave out the company-run airports (Narita, Kansai, Itami, Chubu), so no current rank could be confirmed.

claims.claim: 21.5 million passengers in 2018
claims.why: Eight years old. Replaced by the year to March 2026 (see above).

claims.claim: hub for two airlines that matter for island hopping
claims.wasBefore: It is the hub for two airlines that matter for island hopping.
claims.why: Reworded around Ryukyu Air Commuter alone (see above and below).

claims.claim: Japan Transocean Air connects Okinawa to the rest of Japan
claims.wasBefore: Japan Transocean Air connects Okinawa to the rest of Japan
claims.why: Rests on Wikipedia alone. The terminal operator's airline list shows only that JTA flies here. JTA's site (jal.co.jp) answers plain requests with 403; its home page loaded in the browser but says nothing about bases or routes, and two guessed company-page addresses returned 404, so no further tries.

claims.claim: Malaysia among international markets
claims.why: Not on the terminal operator's list of cities served (see above).

claims.claim: terminals worth identifying before travel
claims.wasBefore: The terminals were built in stages and are worth identifying before travel.
claims.why: Overtaken: a connecting building has joined the domestic and international terminals since 2019 (see above). 'Built in stages' is kept.

claims.claim: low cost carrier terminal, north annex, 2012, for Peach
claims.wasBefore: a low cost carrier terminal was added as a north annex in 2012 for Peach services
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; neither the terminal operator's history nor MLIT's sheet mentions it.

claims.claim: old domestic terminal became the cargo terminal in 2009
claims.wasBefore: The old domestic terminal became the cargo terminal in 2009.
claims.why: Sources disagree: MLIT's sheet has a new cargo terminal building opening in 2009 (平成２１年 新貨物ターミナルビル供用開始), not a converted passenger terminal, and the terminal operator's history does not mention it.

claims.claim: Skytrax 91st in 2024, up from 199th
claims.wasBefore: Skytrax ranked it 91st in the world in 2024, up from 199th the year before

claims.claim: the most improved airport in the world in 2024
claims.wasBefore: making it the most improved airport in the world that year
claims.why: Wrong. Skytrax's World's Most Improved Airport for 2024 was New Chitose (Hokkaido Airports' release of 19 March 2026 and Wikipedia's New Chitose article, both saved for CTS). Wikipedia's Naha article draws the conclusion itself from the jump in rank.

claims.claim: home to a Japan Air Self-Defense Force base
claims.wasBefore: The airport is also home to a Japan Air Self-Defense Force base.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. MLIT's pages on Naha do not mention it, and the defence ministry's site (mod.go.jp) answered a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' bot check when tried for New Chitose, so it was not tried again.

claims.claim: second runway (2,700 m) since March 2020
claims.why: Held back: verified but replaces nothing in the old text. A second runway of 2,700 m opened in March 2020 (Reiwa 2).

claims.claim: China routes cut back sharply since December 2025
claims.why: Held back: one source only. The terminal operator's report for the year to March 2026 says China routes have been sharply reduced since December 2025 because relations between Japan and China worsened, while new and extra Taiwan and Korea flights took international passengers to a record 4.13 million. It could go in as the operator's own statement ('the terminal operator reports...'), but the cause is a fact about Japan-China relations with no second saved source, so it is left for Andy.

opinion.text: so most onward travel in the prefecture starts here
opinion.why: Judgement carried over from the old text: the terminal operator lists flights from Naha to seven other Okinawa islands (Ishigaki, Miyako, Shimojishima, Kumejima, Kitadaito, Minami Daito and Yonaguni), and Ryukyu Air Commuter's island network is centred here.
